nh_monadnock_region.blurb: The Monadnock Region is a spread of well over a dozen climbing areas in New Hampshire, with plenty more to it than its namesake mountain. Bouldering is the main event, with problems from V0 up to V11. Trad and sport routes, from 5.4 into the 5.11s, are found mainly at Bears Den Natural Area and Marlow Profile, and a few spots have top-rope lines. Revolutionary War Boulder and Willard Pond hold the most boulder problems. At Willard Pond the blocks are gritty glacial erratic granite in a quiet, little-visited setting, and winter is the best season there, since cold air suits the texture, with fall and spring also workable.

ok_narrows_the.blurb: The Narrows is a compact cluster of walls in the Wichita Mountains Wildlife Refuge in southwest Oklahoma, where a creek runs beneath tall rock faces. Traditional climbing dominates, with some top-rope and a few sport routes, plus bouldering around the Boulder Picnic Area. Routes run from 5.6 to the low 5.12s, with a healthy supply of moderates up to 5.11. The rock is granite, as it is across the refuge, where climbing is possible year round and spring and fall are the most popular seasons. Zoo Wall has a large prow and roofs, and the rock can be very slick when wet. Lichen Wall and Leaning Tower are the other big walls.

va_m_r_n_r_a.blurb: This is the Mount Rogers National Recreation Area in southwest Virginia, a huge high-country expanse next to Grayson Highlands State Park, with large rock formations, open balds and spruce-fir forest. All of the climbing is bouldering: blocks, slabs and steep vertical faces, with many highball lines. Problems run from very easy to V10, with most between V3 and V6. Approaches are longer than in the state park and the area is little documented, so a visit can easily take a full day. Bearpen Boulders hold the vast majority of the problems, with smaller clusters at Rhododendron Gap and Whitetop.

va_prospectors.blurb: Prospectors is a long cliff line in Breaks Interstate Park in southwest Virginia, split into many distinct crags along a popular trail that runs more than a mile. Sport routes outnumber trad, and the terrain mixes slabs, roofs and overhanging faces with the occasional crack. The park's sandstone is compared to New River Gorge and Obed climbing, and here it is very hard, solid rock. Grades centre on 5.10, with a good number of 5.8 to 5.9 and a solid tier of 5.11 and 5.12. Eastern Prospectors is the busiest section, followed by Mid Prospectors, State Line 2nd Tier and The Homestead.

ca_bowman_valley.blurb: Bowman Valley is a group of secluded crags beneath Bowman Lake Dam in the I-80 corridor near Lake Tahoe, at about 5,500 feet. Sport climbing dominates, with a few top-rope lines, some trad and a handful of boulder problems. The granite is coarsely textured with good friction, ranging from slab to overhanging roofs. Grades centre on 5.10 and 5.11 with a strong 5.12 tier, a spread of easier routes from 5.6 to 5.9, and a couple of 5.13s. The wider Bowman Lake Road area is popular once the snow is gone. The Cove, Larry Land, The Fun House and Boy Scout Wall are the largest crags.
